Re: Reservation of Rights — Claim No. MC-2026-118447
    Insured: Halloran Precision Castings, LLC
    Policy No. CGL-4471982, effective January 1, 2026 to January 1, 2027
    Claimant: Ridgeline Aerospace Components, Inc.

Dear Mr. Halloran:

Meridian Casualty Insurance Company (“Meridian”) has received notice of the lawsuit filed against Halloran Precision Castings, LLC (“Halloran” or “you”) by Ridgeline Aerospace Components, Inc. in the Superior Court of Connecticut, Judicial District of Waterbury (the “Lawsuit”). This letter states Meridian’s position on coverage. Meridian will provide a defense in the Lawsuit, subject to a full reservation of all rights under the Policy and applicable law, as explained below.

1. The Claim.

The complaint alleges that between March and July 2025 Halloran supplied turbine housings that failed dimensional tolerance requirements, that Ridgeline incorporated the housings into assemblies it delivered to its own customers, and that the assemblies were recalled. Ridgeline asserts claims for breach of contract, breach of express warranty, negligent misrepresentation, and negligence, and seeks the cost of the recall, replacement parts, and lost profits.

2. Defense.

Meridian will defend Halloran in the Lawsuit under a reservation of rights. Meridian has appointed Kearns & Whitlock LLP as defense counsel. Meridian’s agreement to defend is not an admission that the Policy affords coverage for any claim, count, or item of damages asserted in the Lawsuit, and it is not a waiver of any policy term, condition, exclusion, or defense.

3. Reservation of Rights.

Meridian reserves all rights under the Policy and applicable law, including the right to: (a) deny indemnity in whole or in part; (b) withdraw from the defense upon reasonable notice if it is determined that no claim in the Lawsuit is potentially covered; (c) seek reimbursement of defense costs advanced for claims that are not covered, to the extent permitted by Connecticut law; and (d) file an action for declaratory judgment as to its rights and obligations under the Policy. Meridian does not waive, and expressly preserves, every coverage position stated in this letter and every position not stated in it.

4. Policy Provisions That May Apply.

Meridian directs your attention to the following provisions of the Policy, which is enclosed in full. This is not an exhaustive list, and Meridian reserves the right to rely on any other provision.

The Insuring Agreement obligates Meridian to pay sums the insured becomes legally obligated to pay as damages because of “bodily injury” or “property damage” caused by an “occurrence.” Ridgeline’s claims may not allege an “occurrence” as that term is defined, because damages arising from the insured’s own defective product are generally understood as a business risk rather than a fortuity.

Exclusion (a) bars coverage for “property damage” expected or intended from the standpoint of the insured. Exclusion (b) bars coverage for damages assumed under contract, except an “insured contract.” Exclusion (k) bars coverage for “property damage” to “your product” arising out of it or any part of it. Exclusion (m) bars coverage for “property damage” to “impaired property” or to property not physically injured, arising out of a defect in “your product.” Exclusion (n) bars damages claimed for the recall, withdrawal, inspection, repair, or replacement of “your product.”

Coverage for lost profits, the cost of replacement parts, and the cost of the recall may therefore be barred in whole or in part. Coverage for the negligent misrepresentation count may also be barred because that count does not allege “bodily injury” or “property damage.”

5. Late Notice.

The Policy requires the insured to notify Meridian as soon as practicable of an occurrence or offense that may result in a claim. Meridian received notice of this matter on July 30, 2026. The complaint was served on Halloran on May 6, 2026. Meridian reserves its rights with respect to the timeliness of notice and any prejudice resulting from it, and it will not raise late notice as a bar without first determining that it was prejudiced.

6. Your Rights.

You have the right to retain independent counsel at your own expense to monitor the defense. If a conflict of interest arises between you and Meridian such that appointed counsel could control the outcome of a coverage issue, you may be entitled to independent counsel at Meridian’s expense under Connecticut law, and Meridian will address that question if it arises. You may also submit any information you believe bears on coverage, and Meridian will consider it.

7. Cooperation.

The Policy requires you to cooperate with Meridian in the investigation and defense of the Lawsuit, to attend hearings and trials, and to assist in securing evidence and obtaining the attendance of witnesses. Please forward all suit papers and correspondence promptly.

8. No Waiver.

No act of Meridian, its employees, or appointed counsel in investigating or defending the Lawsuit shall waive or be construed to waive any right of Meridian under the Policy or at law. Nothing in this letter shall be construed as an admission of coverage or liability.

If you have questions, please contact me directly at (860) 555-0173.
